chunks: The one who sees with the heart, the one who acts with the eyes,
the beginning of his action is that he knows: is his action against him or for him? If it is for him, he proceeds in it, and if it is against him, he stops at it.

For, he who acts without knowledge is like one who travels without a path, so his distance from the clear path only increases his distance from his need, and he who acts with knowledge is like one who travels on the clear path, so let the one who sees see: is he proceeding or returning?!

key_terms.النّاظِرُ بِالْقَلْبِ: The one who sees with the heart (inner insight)
key_terms.الْعَامِلُ بِالْبَصَرِ: The one who acts with the eyes (external action)

ai.seo_question: How does one determine if an action is beneficial or harmful according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali employs the metaphor of the heart as the eye of insight to distinguish between action performed for self-indulgence versus action performed as a duty. He contrasts the blind actor, whose distance from the truth grows with every step, with the knowledgeable traveler on a clear path, urging believers to constantly evaluate whether their deeds are propelling them forward or causing them to retreat. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *taqwa* (God-consciousness) and the integration of *ilm* (knowledge) with *amal* (action) as the foundation of spiritual progress.
